issue.title: Fix SASE commit publication scan hang
issue.description: During finalizer commit for glyph-only compact bead rows, sase_git_commit created and pushed commit 7d4afb394 successfully, then hung for several minutes in post-commit publication. py-spy showed the hot path: run_agent_publication_step -> refresh_committed_plan_header -> build_plan_association_index -> resolve_agent_association_url -> get_reserved_family_names -> registry_file_is_stale -> source_signature_paths -> dismissed_bundles.rglob("*.json"). The process stayed CPU-bound until interrupted; git status was clean and origin/master contained the commit. Investigate caching or bounding dismissed_bundles scanning in agent name registry publication.

payload.entry: Revalidated during open task-bead audit on master d462e97bb. The standard 27-worker just test run spent 124.00s in tests/test_dismissed_bundle_persistence.py::test_save_dismissed_bundle_is_fast_with_many_existing_bundles, matching the recursive dismissed_bundles scan reported in this task and confirming this remains a post-c82eff9a0 recurrence rather than a duplicate of closed sase-c7.

payload.close_reason: I'm pretty sure we already fixed this.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction during post-completion finalizer for commit a39ca1f9d: sase_git_commit printed create_commit completed successfully and skipped prompt archive publication because raw_xprompt.md was unavailable, then stayed CPU-bound for several minutes in post-commit publication. py-spy showed run_agent_publication_step -> refresh_committed_plan_header -> build_plan_association_index -> resolve_agent_association_url -> get_reserved_family_names -> registry_file_is_stale -> source_signature_paths -> dismissed_bundles.rglob('*.json'); Ctrl-C produced the same traceback at dismissed_bundles.rglob. git status was clean and origin/master contained a39ca1f9d after interruption.

Independent reproduction during post-completion finalizer for commit fa43d2f46: sase_git_commit printed create_commit completed successfully and pushed the commit to origin/master, then stayed CPU-bound for over four minutes in post-commit publication. py-spy showed run_agent_publication_step -> refresh_committed_plan_header -> build_plan_association_index -> resolve_agent_association_url -> get_reserved_family_names -> registry_file_is_stale -> source_signature_paths -> iter_agent_artifact_dirs; Ctrl-C traceback ended in iter_agent_artifact_dirs. git status was clean and origin/master contained fa43d2f46 after interruption.

Independent reproduction during post-completion finalizer for commit 4fcaee95a5e543fd6635fc820e64b3cd2776480d: sase_git_commit printed create_commit completed successfully and pushed HEAD to origin/master, then stayed CPU-bound in post-commit publication. Ctrl-C traceback showed run_agent_publication_step -> refresh_committed_plan_header -> build_plan_association_index -> get_reserved_family_names -> registry_file_is_stale. A bounded 'sase_git_commit --resume' replay reproduced the same stall in plan-header publication; git status remained clean and HEAD matched origin/master.

Independent reproduction during post-completion finalizer for commit e257d6b1b: sase_git_commit printed create_commit completed successfully, skipped prompt archive publication because raw_xprompt.md was unavailable, and pushed HEAD to origin/master, then remained CPU-bound for over five minutes in post-commit tracking/publication. Ctrl-C traceback showed run_agent_publication_step -> refresh_committed_plan_header -> build_plan_association_index -> resolve_agent_association_url -> get_reserved_family_names -> registry_file_is_stale -> _source_signature -> path.stat. git status was clean and HEAD matched origin/master after interruption.
